13                RABBI BUTMAN:   Let us pray.  

14                {In Hebrew}  Our heavenly Father, 

15   please bestow Your benevolence on the members of 

16   the New York State Senate.  

17                Bless them personally, and their 

18   families, with all good things, so that they 

19   should be able to serve You and people in the 

20   State of New York faithfully as they have until 

21   now, especially if today or lately the members 

22   of the New York State Senate have passed a 

23   resolution honoring the Rebbe, the Lubavitcher 

24   Rebbe, Rabbi Menachem M. Schneerson, with 114 

25   days of education, commemorating 114 years since 


                                                                1965

 1   the birth of the Rebbe.  

 2                The Rebbe cared for the education 

 3   of each child regardless of race, religion, 

 4   color or creed.  I heard the Rebbe say many 

 5   times that he wants each child to know that 

 6   there is an Eye that sees and there is an Ear 

 7   that hears, and that the world is not a jungle.

 8                In 1991, before I went to 

 9   Washington to open the United States Senate -- 

10   which is a branch, of course of this Senate -- I 

11   went to see the Rebbe.  And the Rebbe said to 

12   me:  "Take with you a tzedakah box, a charity 

13   box.  And during your prayer you should offer $1 

14   into the charity box.  And everybody should see 

15   what you are doing, and they should know what 

16   money should be used for."  

17                So it is my unique pleasure today, 

18   and privilege, to do what the Rebbe told me.  

19   And I'm putting in a dollar, on which it says 

20   "In God We Trust," into the pushkeh, into the 

21   charity box right now.  And I would invite each 

22   and every one of you, if you want, to 

23   participate as well.  

24                But I don't want you to think that 

25   this is a fundraising campaign.  Because if it

 2                SENATOR LITTLE:   Thank you, 

 3   Mr. President.  

 4                I would like to thank all who are 

 5   supporting this piece of legislation.  It's a new 

 6   bill, and what it actually does is require that 

 7   when you go and have your car inspected on an 

 8   annual basis, the person inspecting the car 

 9   checks with the website where you -- it's called 

10   safercar.gov, a federal website, and it will 

11   indicate whether or not you have an active recall 

12   on that car.  And then on your inspection report, 

13   you will get the message, yes, you have an active 

14   recall on your car, and this is the recall.  

15                And the reason for doing this is 

16   that very often cars are sold -- and I know I 

17   have sold a car, traded it in, and then months 

18   later get a recall notice on the car that I 

19   already sold, which you throw away.

20                So this is a way -- and especially 

21   if you've bought a car from a relative, a friend, 

22   there's no record, a quick record so that you 

23   get a recall immediately.

24                We know that there's one 

25   manufacturer who has just sent out more recalls 


                                                                1976

 1   about an airbag that can spit out kind of 

 2   material, sharp items from it.  And many, many 

 3   more cars are being recalled.  In 2015, 

 4   51 million vehicles had a recall on them.

 5                So this is one way of having an 

 6   annual reminder.  It's up to the person to go and 

 7   do something about it, take their car to a 

 8   manufacturer who will fix the car for free.  

 9                And I think it's a good bill, and I 

10   appreciate support for it.

11                Thank you very much.

19                SENATOR RITCHIE:   Thank you,

21                Right now in New York State we have 

22   over 10,000 men, women and children currently 

23   waiting for a lifesaving organ transplant.  And 

24   unfortunately, in New York about every 15 hours 

25   someone passes away while waiting for a 


                                                                1978

 1   lifesaving organ transplant.  

 2                And what makes matters worse here in 

 3   New York is we lag behind almost every state in 

 4   the nation when it comes to the percentage of 

 5   people that are eligible, that are actually 

 6   enrolled in the organ donor program.  Lauren's 

 7   Law, this legislation that we're voting on right 

 8   now to make permanent, is an effort to change 

 9   that.  

10                It's named after a young girl named 

11   Lauren Shields who, when she was 9 years old, she 

12   spent 15 days on life support waiting for a 

13   lifesaving heart transplant.  And she's one of 

14   the lucky ones.  She received that lifesaving 

15   heart transplant in the nick of time.  And since 

16   then, she has spoken to anyone that she can about 

17   her ordeal, her experience.  And she'd be here 

18   today, but she's studying for exams in school.  

19   But she wanted to be here.

20                But what we're trying to do is make 

21   it permanent.  When we originally passed this 

22   bill, it took effect October 3, 2013.  And what 

23   it does is very simple.  We found that over 

24   97 percent of the people that enroll in the organ 

25   donor program do it through the Department of 


                                                                1979

 1   Motor Vehicles.  So hey, we don't have to 

 2   recreate the wheel, let's just do what other 

 3   states already do and incorporate that in 

 4   New York State.  

 5                So now when you go to the DMV, 

 6   you're asked a question:  Would you like to be an 

 7   organ donor?  Yes, or skip the question.  

 8                And since October 3rd of 2013 when 

 9   this bill took effect -- and thanks to Senator 

10   Hannon, with some tweaks and amendments -- we've 

11   seen the numbers increase.  We've actually seen a 

12   60 percent increase in the percentage of people 

13   that actually enroll.  

14                And we believe that just in the next 

15   four years, by keeping Lauren's Law going, we're 

16   going to enroll another half a million people.  

17   Those are the numbers that we predict.  

18                Now, what this bill would do is make 

19   Lauren's Law permanent, so it doesn't have to 

20   come before us every few years, but makes sure 

21   that that's a permanent change so we can move 

22   forward in saving people's lives.

23                So I want to thank Senator Flanagan, 

24   Majority Leader Flanagan for really pushing these 

25   issues; Senator Serino and Senator Hannon, who
